canonical_name: Pila-Wilkie theorem (rational-point counting in o-minimal structures)
canonical_statement: Provisional source-faithful root: for a set X definable in an o-minimal expansion of the real field and every positive epsilon, the number of rational points of height at most T in the transcendental part X minus its algebraic part is at most c(X, epsilon) times T^epsilon, for the source theorem's admissible T.
domain_and_universes: An o-minimal expansion of the ordered real field; a definable X subset of R^n; epsilon > 0; height cutoff T. Exact Lean universes and structures are not frozen.
hypotheses: the ambient expansion of the real field is o-minimal
X is definable in that structure
conclusion: The bounded-height rational-point counting function on the transcendental part of X is at most c * T^epsilon.
excluded_or_unresolved_variants: replacement of the algebraic part by a Zariski closure or an arbitrary exceptional set
degenerate_cases: Empty and zero-dimensional sets should be consequences of the root, not alternate roots. The exact conventions for T below 1, height zero, and epsilon equal to zero remain open; epsilon = 0 is not admitted by the source-shaped claim.
foundation_profile: Not instantiated at intake; classical logic, choice, quotient, real-analysis, definability, and finiteness dependencies require audit.
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel profile intended; exact toolchain and transitive dependency closure remain open.

source_revisions: Primary discovery anchor: J. Pila and A. J. Wilkie, The rational points of a definable set, Duke Math. J. 133 (2006), no. 3, 591-616, Theorem 1.8, DOI 10.1215/S0012-7094-06-13336-7. Immutable file hash and errata review remain open.
